solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hit wood on Birkdale's first

indicators.note: in an across clue, wood on a letter means the wood comes after it
Birkdale's first means the opening letter of that word is taken

parts.note: ash is a tree and so a kind of wood

explanation.surface: A golf shot struck with a wooden club on the first hole at Royal Birkdale.
explanation.walkthrough: Birkdale is a famous English golf course, so 'wood' and 'Hit' both pull towards golf; the wood here is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To bash something is to strike it hard, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Talk spitefully about side with incisiveness

parts.note: the back is one side of something
bite means sharpness or incisive force

explanation.surface: Gossiping maliciously about a team with a cutting edge.
explanation.definitionFit: To backbite is to malign someone behind their back.

clue.text: Anecdote beginning to shock Conservative

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of the word shock

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A tale that starts out shocking a traditionalist.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short tale, a story told of a real event.

clue.text: Taken by surprise, the old lady retired, exhausted

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the word for the old lady is read backwards

parts.note: MA is a familiar word for mother, one's old lady
bushed is informal for worn out

explanation.surface: Mother has gone to bed worn out, startled by something.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ambushed is to be attacked without warning, so caught unawares.

clue.text: Extra short on top of beer brings confidence

indicators.note: in a down clue, on top of puts the first piece above the second
short means lacking its tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: more means extra or additional
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: An extra round of beer boosts a drinker's confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Morale is the spirit or self-assurance of a person or group.

clue.text: Downright incompetent?

definitions.meaning: ... means absolute or total, as in an ... success
... also means lacking the qualifications for a job

explanation.surface: Is someone simply hopeless at the job?
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both utter, without reservation, and lacking proper credentials.

clue.text: Woman who expects to succeed?

parts.note: succeed reads as achieve success, but here it means follow on, inheriting a title or estate

explanation.surface: An ambitious woman confident of success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeed' is taken in its sense of coming next in line.
explanation.definitionFit: She is a female heir, due to inherit property or rank when its holder dies.

clue.text: Left after outstanding contest

indicators.note: after places the left letter following the other piece

parts.note: a debt outstanding is due, still to be paid

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned after a remarkable competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' suggests excellent; here it means unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: A duel is a combat or contest between two parties.

clue.text: Thick soup cowherd prepared

indicators.note: prepared suggests the letters are made ready in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A herdsman has cooked up a thick soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Chowder is a hearty, creamy soup, often made with clams or fish.

clue.text: Large drink on American's bill to verify

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a double is a twice-sized measure of spirits
check is the American word for a restaurant bill

explanation.surface: Checking the tab after ordering a big drink in a US bar.
explanation.definitionFit: To double-check is to confirm again that something is correct.

clue.text: Completely gave up nicotine at the end

parts.note: to quit is to give up, here in the past tense

indicators.note: at the end picks the final letter of the word nicotine

explanation.surface: Someone finally stopped smoking for good.
explanation.definitionFit: Quite in its older sense means entirely or wholly, as in 'quite finished'.

clue.text: Love a rye — buy supply, with permission from you

indicators.note: supply is read as the adverb of supple, flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: A drinker loves rye whisky and wants to buy a stock of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a noun or verb about provisions, but here it is supple-ly, 'in a flexible way', signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a polite formula asking leave, meaning if you allow it.

clue.text: Mean to collect brief legal document towards the end of the day?

definitions.text: towards the end of the day?

indicators.note: to collect means to take in, so the mean word holds the other inside

parts.note: tight means stingy

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a will is a legal document setting out a bequest

explanation.surface: A stingy lawyer picks up a short document late in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' looks like a lawyer's brief but cuts WILL to WIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilight is the dim half-light just after sunset, as evening approaches.

clue.text: Toy weapon on edge of seat

indicators.note: in an across clue, the weapon placed on a letter comes after it
edge of picks an outer letter, here the last one of seat

parts.note: a rifle is a firearm

explanation.surface: A toy gun left perched on the side of a chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toy' looks like a noun but is the verb: to toy with is to trifle with.
explanation.definitionFit: To trifle is to toy or play idly with something, treating it lightly.

clue.text: Lethargy shown in Iran tie, unexpectedly

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests things turning out differently, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sluggish performance in a football match involving Iran ends in a surprise draw.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is sluggishness, an unwillingness to move or act.

clue.text: Talk at length about GI's cryptic puzzle

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the talk is placed around the other letters

parts.note: to jaw is to talk on and on

indicators.note: cryptic means obscure or scrambled, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Chatter about a soldier's crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' sounds like part of the puzzle's description, but it is the anagram signal; the apostrophe in GI's is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A jigsaw is a picture puzzle of interlocking pieces.

clue.text: Trim conifer

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means neat and smart

explanation.surface: Prune a pine.
explanation.definitionFit: One word serves as both smart in appearance and a type of fir-like tree.

clue.text: Remarkable bar next to Hebridean island lake

indicators.note: next to places one piece directly beside the next

parts.note: bar as a preposition means except
Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland
L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A striking pub found beside a loch on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' reads as a pub but works as the preposition 'except'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exceptional is out of the ordinary and worthy of note.

clue.text: One is blown to produce sound

indicators.note: blown means blasted apart, so the letters scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: A wind instrument is played to make music.
explanation.definitionFit: A noise is any sound, especially a loud one.

clue.text: Luxurious hotel not appearing to give credit

indicators.note: not appearing means absent, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: plush means sumptuous or luxurious
H is the abbreviation for hotel, as on maps and in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A smart hotel is missing from the listings, which earns it praise.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is an advantage or point in one's favour, a credit.

clue.text: Large Italian male, loose-limbed

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A big Italian man who moves with an easy, flexible grace.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe means supple and agile, with a flexible body.

clue.text: Downfall caused by murder in a French gîte, primarily

indicators.note: in places the murder inside the other letters

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of the word gîte

parts.note: to do in is slang for to kill

explanation.surface: A killing in a French holiday cottage brought someone to ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: A gîte is a French holiday home.
explanation.definitionFit: One's undoing is the cause of ruin or collapse.

clue.text: Jewel box presented by King Lear, Cordelia ultimately rejected

parts.note: to spar is to box in practice
K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: rejected means thrown out, so a letter is removed from the name
ultimately picks the final letter of the name Cordelia

explanation.surface: King Lear disowns his daughter Cordelia, as in Shakespeare's tragedy, while a jewel box changes hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' drops A (Cordelia's last letter) from LEAR to leave LER.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparkler is informal slang for a diamond or other gem that glitters.

clue.text: Enthusiasm shown during quizzes there

indicators.note: shown during says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Eagerness on display at the pub quiz.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest means keen relish or gusto for something.
